claim: On hard328 problems where a cued-base sample finished wrong (boxed answer within the cap, graded wrong), the rank-1 edit (top-1 direction per matrix of the RL-Math 3.1 delta, 1x) is right no more often than a second cued-base sample, while the directions-2-8 edit at 1.5x is right clearly more often: direction 1 adds finishes, not right answers on problems the base already finishes.
why_only_this: None of the other top mechanisms splits the RL delta by singular direction. The sampling mechanisms (round-09/grader-m01, run-08/f2-m01) only predict regression to the mean on selected problems, and that is the same for every edit; the second base sample removes it. The cap and grader mechanisms (run-08/f2-m02, round-09/grader-m06, run-08/f2-m06, round-09/training-m01, run-04/f2-m05) are about how unfinished or misplaced answers are scored, so they predict nothing about base-finished-wrong problems. round-09/grader-m04 and round-10/problems-m04 predict that an edit's right-answer gain sits on mid-difficulty problems and its cap change sits in the long tail, but they give no reason why direction 1 should have no right-answer gain while directions 2-8 have one. Under any of them, an edit that lifts the hard328 total by 17 (181 vs 164) should also raise the right rate on finished-wrong problems in rough proportion. Only this mechanism predicts a near-zero gain for direction 1 next to a clear gain for directions 2-8 on the same problems.
computation: 1) Load per-problem hard328 rows (problem index 0-327, right under grader v3, cap hit / finished flag, tokens, extracted answer) for these cells: (a) selector: cued base, T 1.0, sample 0, results/day1/hard328_base_cue_t10-01 (164 right, 77 cap hits); (b) second base: the four samples in results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01; (c) TOP1: base + 1 direction per matrix of the RL-Math delta at 1x (posted 181/328, cap hits 51), its run folder under results/xreward/edits; (d) D28: base + directions 2-8 at 1.5x (posted 183/328, cap hits 69), its folder under results/xreward/depth3 or results/xreward/edits; (e) references: top-8 at 1.5x and matched random rank-8 (158/328) from results/xreward/edits, plus TOP1 at 2x (184/328) if it is stored. If a cell's per-problem rows are not in its run folder, take them from results/table/hard328-02 (per-problem rows of every committed configuration). Before going on, check that each cell's right count and cap-hit count match the posted numbers; stop and report any mismatch. Use studies/theory/results/direct/dial-01 (readout.json, m1x_hard328_rows.jsonl) as the template for the row format and for how 'finished wrong' was defined in result-124593, and use the same definition. 2) For each of the four second-base samples, compare its text hash or tokens and its answer to the selector row. Drop any sample that is the same draw as the selector. 3) Set S = the problems where the selector row finished (no cap hit, an answer extracted) and is graded wrong. Report |S| (expected about 87). 4) For each problem i in S, set b_i = the mean right indicator over the remaining second-base samples, t_i = the TOP1 right indicator, d_i = the D28 right indicator. Count a capped edit row as wrong. 5) Compute E_top1 = 100*mean(t_i - b_i) and E_d28 = 100*mean(d_i - b_i) in points, and G = E_d28 - E_top1. Compute each the same way for the top-8 1.5x reference (it should reproduce about +13.5 from result-124593), for the random rank-8 control and, if stored, for TOP1 2x. 6) Get 95% intervals from a paired bootstrap over the problems in S: 10,000 resamples, numpy default_rng(seed=0), percentile intervals, with E_top1, E_d28 and G computed on the same resample. 7) Repeat for every selector-sample pair as a robustness check: each of the 4+1 base samples serves as selector in turn, the others serve as second base, and problems are pooled with a cluster bootstrap by problem. Report it, but the verdict uses step 6. 8) Also report the finished-row precision (right / finished) of base, TOP1, D28 over all 328 problems, and the number of TOP1 rows with no boxed answer, as context only.
refuted_if: The rank-1 edit itself adds right answers on base-finished-wrong problems: the lower end of the 95% interval of E_top1 is at least the threshold. The claim is also refuted if directions 2-8 do not beat direction 1 on these problems: the upper end of the 95% interval of G = E_d28 - E_top1 is at or below 0.
threshold: E_top1 95% lower bound >= +5.0 points (refutes); or G 95% upper bound <= 0.0 points (refutes). The claim holds if neither happens and the E_top1 point estimate is below half the E_d28 point estimate.
null: The second cued-base sample on the same selected problems. It removes regression to the mean and is stronger than a random baseline. As a second null, the matched random rank-8 edit run through the same computation must give an excess near 0. As a positive control, the top-8 1.5x edit must reproduce about +13.5 points (result-124593). The contrast that decides is TOP1 against directions 2-8, two edits built from the same RL delta.
